pages.title: Why We Built Tempo First
body: What is the smallest useful interface for protecting attention?
Tempo taught us that workflow tools should remove negotiation, not add dashboards.
A focused ritual can become infrastructure for better work.

pages.title: The Listener Becomes the Phantom
body: Who is The Phantom: a character we tell stories about, or a state of mind the listener becomes?
The Locksmith is not about breaking in. It is about becoming someone who can build anything.
Every track will represent a stage in the transformation from ordinary to extraordinary.
When someone presses play, they do not just listen. They step into a different identity.
One insight rippled through every decision.

pages.title: From Friction to Flow
body: Friction is not always bad; unchosen friction is the problem.
Every removed decision gives attention back to the work that matters.
Beautiful constraints are a kindness to future focus.

pages.title: Continuo Isn’t Another Productivity App
body: Productivity apps often preserve motion instead of meaning.
Continuo should help people continue the right work, not merely track more work.
The tool is successful when the user returns to the craft faster.

pages.title: Cold Boot Defines the Identity
body: The first sound should feel like a system waking up and remembering its purpose.
Cold Boot becomes the threshold: before it, potential; after it, commitment.
Identity lands better when it is introduced as a ritual instead of an explanation.
